Items: [{"id":"cap-v2-ordering_and_selection-go-generation-01","specification":"Implement a submission-ranking API in Go.

Use package `solution` and provide this public API:

```go
type Submission struct {
    SubmissionID  string
    Title         string
    JuryPoints    int
    AudiencePoints int
}

func RankSubmissions(input []Submission) []Submission
```

Multiple input values may have the same `SubmissionID`. Emit exactly one submission per ID. For each duplicated ID, select the submission with the greatest `JuryPoints`; if tied, select the one with the greatest `AudiencePoints`; if still tied, select the lexicographically smaller `Title`. Candidates still tied after these comparisons are identical for all relevant fields.

Rank the selected submissions by descending `JuryPoints`, then descending `AudiencePoints`, then ascending `Title`, then ascending `SubmissionID`. Return an empty non-nil slice for empty input.

The implementation must be deterministic and use only the Go standard library. Do not perform filesystem, network, clock, or random operations. Return a complete source file without a `main` function.

Return only the complete source file; do not include Markdown fences or prose.","assigned_primary_capability":"ordering_and_selection","primary_capability_definition":"rank, sort, select, merge, or prioritize values with explicit deterministic tie behavior","scheduled_cross_cutting_dimension":"duplicate_handling"},{"id":"cap-v2-ordering_and_selection-go-generation-02","specification":"Implement an API that merges ranked search-result batches.

Use package `solution` and provide this public API:

```go
type SearchResult struct {
    URL        string
    Title      string
    Source     string
    Confidence int
}

func MergeSearchResults(batches [][]SearchResult) []SearchResult
```

A URL identifies a result, so the output must contain at most one value for each URL even when that URL occurs in different batches or sources. Among values with the same URL, retain the one with greater `Confidence`; on a tie, retain the one with lexicographically smaller `Source`; on another tie, retain the one with lexicographically smaller `Title`.

Order retained results by descending `Confidence`, ascending `Title`, ascending `URL`, and finally ascending `Source`. Fully tied values are identical. Return an empty non-nil slice when no results are supplied.

Use only the Go standard library. Do not perform I/O, networking, clock access, or random operations. Return a complete source file without a `main` function.

```go
package solution

import "sort"

type Document struct {
	ID      string
	Quality int
	Cost    int
}

func RankDocuments(documents []Document) []Document {
	result := documents
	sort.SliceStable(result, func(i, j int) bool {
		if result[i].Quality != result[j].Quality {
			return result[i].Quality > result[j].Quality
		}
		if result[i].Cost != result[j].Cost {
			return result[i].Cost < result[j].Cost
		}
		return result[i].ID < result[j].ID
	})
	return result
}
```

Correct it and return one complete Go source file using package `solution` and the same public API.

Documents must be ordered by descending `Quality`, ascending `Cost`, then ascending `ID`. Documents tied on all three fields must retain their original relative order. `RankDocuments` must not mutate the input slice, and the returned slice must have independent backing storage so changing an element in the result cannot change the input. For empty input, return an empty non-nil slice.

Use only the Go standard library. Do not perform filesystem, network, clock, or random operations. Do not add a `main` function.

```go
package solution

import "sort"

type Chapter struct {
	Code       string
	Section    int
	Importance int
	Keywords   []string
}

func OrderChapters(chapters []Chapter) []Chapter {
	result := make([]Chapter, len(chapters))
	copy(result, chapters)
	sort.SliceStable(result, func(i, j int) bool {
		if result[i].Section != result[j].Section {
			return result[i].Section < result[j].Section
		}
		if result[i].Importance != result[j].Importance {
			return result[i].Importance > result[j].Importance
		}
		return result[i].Code < result[j].Code
	})
	return result
}
```

Return one corrected, complete Go source file in package `solution`, preserving the public API.

Preserve nil `Keywords` as nil, and return an empty non-nil result for empty input.

Use package `solution` and provide this public API:

```go
    Name string
    Rank int
    Note string
}

func ParseBadgeManifest(text string) ([]Badge, error)
```

The manifest consists of LF-separated lines. Empty lines are ignored. Every non-empty line must contain exactly three fields separated by literal `|` bytes:

```text
encoded-name|rank|encoded-note
```

`encoded-name` and `encoded-note` use percent encoding: `%` must be followed by exactly two hexadecimal digits representing one byte. Decode these fields using URL path semantics, so `+` remains `+`. Encoded bytes may form UTF-8 text, including an encoded `|`. The decoded name must be non-empty, while the decoded note may be empty. Both decoded strings must be valid UTF-8.

`rank` must contain only ASCII decimal digits and represent an integer from 0 through 100 inclusive. A wrong field count, bad percent escape, invalid UTF-8, empty name, invalid rank syntax, overflow, or out-of-range rank must return a non-nil error and no partial result. Preserve record order and return an empty non-nil slice for an empty manifest.

Use only the Go standard library. Do not access the filesystem, network, clock, or randomness. Return a complete source file without a `main` function.
